notes:
Five pages opened (budget 2-5). Cliopatria has no Saxony row; the East Franks (850-910) and Kingdom of Germany (911-961) rows draw all Germany as one shape, so the stem duchy is drawn from the gazetteer region 'Old Saxony' (confidence 1; it includes the Rhineland part of North Rhine-Westphalia and Sachsen-Anhalt east of the Saale, both too much) minus the Danish land north of Holstein. Not settled: (a) what Saxony lost in Northalbingia/Wagria in 983 and regained later (Duchy page dates only the rising); (b) the Ascanian rump of 1180 and Bernhard of Anhalt's lands (page silent; region read from 1296); (c) the Northern March and the Billung March after 983 (Brandenburg, Holstein under Adolf of Schauenburg are other states); (d) Henry the Lion's deposition year, 1180 in the infobox against 1181 in the text. The page-fetch tool returns an extraction by a small model, so quoted sentences are as returned. Gazetteer lacks Arnsberg, Lauenburg and Lüneburg (coordinates used). Counterparts needing dossiers: duchy-of-westphalia (Cologne), duchy-of-brunswick-luneburg.

Repair of 2026-10-25 (review findings): (1) the Aachen and Cologne circles are out of every shape; the Altmark leaves in 965 as a loss to northern-march (Duchy of Saxony page: 'northeastern Saxon regions', 'later known as Altmark', entrusted to Count Thiadricus after 965; the Northern March page is silent on the Saxon duke's authority over it), so the keyframes are now 911-964, 965-1159, 1160-1166 and 1167-1179; northern-march has no matching loss mirror on its side (its found counterpart is 'March of Gero') and its dossier was not touched. (2) Magdeburg and Bremen are successors with 1180 loss events; the Duchy of Saxony page lists both among the states of the former duchy but names no 1180 grant, so the link rests on their own found events. (3) Mecklenburg is cut at the Peene by a polygon (the pages name no place relative to the river). (4) The Ascanian rump: Duchy of Saxony page gives Lauenburg and Wittenberg (confidence 2); Saxe-Wittenberg says small mostly Eastphalian fringes and names the two only in 1212: disagreement kept. (5) Pribislav page silent after 1167; the 1180 end of the Saxon overlordship stays a bridge at confidence 1.
